cards.explanation: The first reason is that He is good. Right there in the opening line: "Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good…" (Psalm 107:1) The psalm starts with goodness before it tells a single story. I love that, friends. Everything after it is the proof.

The answer is False. The psalm says His loving devotion "endures forever." (Psalm 107:1) Nothing in that line sets a limit or asks anyone to earn it. It just keeps going, and that's good news for every one of us.

The answer is the hand of the enemy. The psalm says the LORD redeemed them "…from the hand of the enemy" (Psalm 107:2). Redeemed is the word the psalm uses for them. Anybody who's come through a tough spot can lift a hand on that one.

The answer is False. He gathered them "…from the lands, from east and west, from north and south." (Psalm 107:3) That's every direction on the compass. No spot on the map is too far for Him to gather someone from.

The answer is True. The wanderers are in desert wastelands, "…finding no path to a city in which to dwell." (Psalm 107:4) They have somewhere to get to, but no way to get there. That's a hard spot to be in.

The answer is the LORD. They "…cried out to the LORD in their trouble…" (Psalm 107:6) They don't wait until things get better first. They cry out right in the middle of the trouble. And the psalm says He delivered them from their distress.

The answer is straight. The verse says, "He led them on a straight path to reach a city where they could live." (Psalm 107:7) Earlier they were finding no path to a city, and now He leads them on a straight one. That's quite a change from wandering the wastelands, friends.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "For He satisfies the thirsty and fills the hungry with good things." (Psalm 107:9) Hungry and thirsty is exactly how those wanderers started out. Now the psalm says why thanks is in order.

The answer is False. The prisoners were in affliction and chains "…because they rebelled against the words of God and despised the counsel of the Most High." (Psalm 107:11) That's the reason the text gives. The good news is still ahead, because the LORD answers their cry.
The answer is that He breaks them away. He "…broke away their chains." (Psalm 107:14) Broken away, not loosened or trimmed. Those chains don't get a second chance.

The answer is the gates of bronze. "For He has broken down the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron." (Psalm 107:16) Bronze gates and iron bars are about as locked as it gets. And He goes through both. That's the reason given this time for the thanks line in verse 15.

The answer is True. "They loathed all food and drew near to the gates of death." (Psalm 107:18) Loathed is a strong word for how they felt about food. I think that tells you how serious things were. It's a heavy moment, and the next verse brings the turn.
The answer is death. The psalm says "…the gates of death." (Psalm 107:18) They drew near to it. And the very next verse shows where they turn: they cried out to the LORD (Psalm 107:19).

The answer is that He sends forth His word. The verse says, "He sent forth His word and healed them; He rescued them from the Pit." (Psalm 107:20) His word is what He sends, and the healing comes with it. The same verse says He rescued them from the Pit.

The answer is to offer sacrifices and tell His works. The psalm says, "Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and declare His works with rejoicing." (Psalm 107:22) Sacrifices and telling His works go together there. The thanks gets said out loud, and with joy, friends.

The answer is deep. The psalm says "…His wonders in the deep." (Psalm 107:24) These traders are out on the mighty waters, and they see what the LORD does there. The deep is where those wonders show up. Plenty to look at.

The answer is a tempest. "For He spoke and raised a tempest that lifted the waves of the sea." (Psalm 107:25) A tempest is a big storm, and the psalm says it comes at His word. That's why it counts among the wonders out there.
The answer is False. The psalm says "…all their skill was useless." (Psalm 107:27) They reel and stagger, and their skill gets them nowhere. Then they cry out to the LORD, and He brings them out.

The answer is that He calms it to a whisper. "He calmed the storm to a whisper, and the waves of the sea were hushed." (Psalm 107:29) From a tempest to a whisper, and the waves go quiet. That's a big change. The next verse says they rejoiced in the silence (Psalm 107:30).
The answer is rejoice. The psalm says, "They rejoiced in the silence…" (Psalm 107:30) The waves are hushed, and the sailors are glad. And then He guides them to the harbor they desired.

The answer is the people and the elders. The verse says, "Let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people and praise Him in the council of the elders." (Psalm 107:32) Both the gathering of the people and the council of the elders are named. The psalm calls for praise out in the open, friends.

The answer is its people's wickedness. He turns fruitful land into fields of salt "…because of the wickedness of its dwellers." (Psalm 107:34) The psalm names the reason right there. Nothing is left to guess about.

The answer is True. The verse says, "He turns a desert into pools of water and a dry land into flowing springs." (Psalm 107:35) Verse 33 says He turns rivers into deserts, and this one goes the other direction. Dry land becomes flowing springs.

The answer is False. "He blesses them, and they multiply greatly; He does not let their herds diminish." (Psalm 107:38) The people multiply greatly, and He does not let the herds diminish. The blessing covers the herds too.

The answer is that He makes them wander a wasteland. He "…pours out contempt on the nobles and makes them wander in a trackless wasteland." (Psalm 107:40) A trackless wasteland means no path to follow. That's quite a turn for nobles.

The answer is needy. The verse says, "But He lifts the needy from affliction and increases their families like flocks." (Psalm 107:41) The needy get lifted from affliction, and their families increase like flocks. It's a good contrast with the nobles in the verse before, friends.
The answer is False. The psalm says, "The upright see and rejoice…" (Psalm 107:42) They watch what the LORD has done, and they're glad. Mourning isn't what this verse says.

The answer is the one who is wise. "Let him who is wise pay heed to these things and consider the loving devotion of the LORD." (Psalm 107:43) The psalm ends by pointing to the wise. And what they're told to consider is His loving devotion.
